newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PolyGram to strengthen TV activities.
newsitem.headline: PolyGram to strengthen TV activities.

text.p: Music and movies group PolyGram NV said on Wednesday it had appointed Bob Sanitsky as president of a newly formed television division.

The company, majority owned by Philips Electronics NV, said in a statement Sanitsky had responsibility for building PolyGram Television into an operation able to develop and distribute a full range of programming for network, cable and syndication in the U.S. and around the world.
The move will strengthen PolyGram's existing television unit ITC, which distributes films and television series such as "Thunderbirds" and "The Prisoner".
PolyGram Television will be based in Los Angeles and use the existing ITC infrastructure, adding 15 staff to the current 50 employed by ITC, which was acquired in 1995.
Sanitsky, who has worked for ICM, Orion TV and Warner Television, said he was looking forward to building a television division at PolyGram.

"PolyGram believes that original television programming is an important part of its visual activities. A very significant part of the value of new film production lies in those films' value for television and the same is true for film and television libraries," the company said in a statement.
